title: President and CEO at Biogen

title: President and CEO at Biogen

speaker: Chris Viehbacher
title: President and CEO at Biogen

We look to our major opportunity with LEQEMBI. As you know, over the past few years since launch, a lot has been done to try to improve the care pathway, make it easier for both physicians and patients.

speaker: Chris Viehbacher
title: President and CEO at Biogen

speaker: Chris Viehbacher
title: President and CEO at Biogen

What I think a lot of people forget is that geographic atrophy is really an autoimmune disease. It is caused by the formation of lesions as a result of aberrant immune activity. What we're really trying to do with geographic atrophy is to prevent the growth of these lesions. When people start talking about visual acuity, that's probably gonna be very difficult because the eye tends to adjust around these lesions.

speaker: Chris Viehbacher
title: President and CEO at Biogen
msg: What really is the goal of treatment is to prevent progression of the disease, which could potentially lead to blindness. I think there's a lot that we need to do in terms of thinking about how we really position this drug and where the benefit is. EMPAVELI, you know, is an enormous benefit to us. We have greater conviction every day on felzartamab, and we look forward to seeing the first data, and hopefully that those data will realize our aspirations for this product. You know, if you went back six, seven years ago, nobody was interested in nephrology.

speaker: Chris Viehbacher
title: President and CEO at Biogen

We'll be present in the nephrology offices, building those relationships, going to congresses now with a marketed product and not a future product.

speaker: Chris Viehbacher
title: President and CEO at Biogen
msg: We believe both in the growth of EMPAVELI, but what that can do for a whole nephrology franchise at Biogen, and we're pretty excited about that, I have to say. But I think it's also fair to say that within Biogen, I think we can probably bring more resources to really support those teams. You know, I don't see a big inflection in SYFOVRE, for example, but I do think there is an opportunity for a growing product there.

speaker: Chris Viehbacher
title: President and CEO at Biogen

speaker: Chris Viehbacher

speaker: Priya Singhal

speaker: Priya Singhal

speaker: Chris Viehbacher
title: President and CEO at Biogen
msg: Priya?

speaker: Priya Singhal
title: Head of Development at Biogen
msg: Thanks, Brian. Just stepping back, you know, BIIB080 is an antisense oligonucleotide. It addresses tau and aims to reduce tau. It was a small trial, but it was very encouraging, which prompted us to get to a proof of concept study. That is what the CELIA readout will tell us. Because this is a pioneering effort, and what we're looking to see is whether reduction of tau leads to and translates into a clinical benefit, specifically on cognition. As we do that, we're exploring several dosing regimens, several treatment frequencies.

speaker: Priya Singhal
title: Head of Development at Biogen
msg: We'll be looking at the totality of data. We're expecting the data sometime mid-year, and I think our goal would be to look at the data and then communicate it and present it, you know, at upcoming forums. That's the plan.

speaker: Brian Abrahams
title: Analyst at RBC Capital Markets

speaker: Priya Singhal
title: Head of Development at Biogen

speaker: Priya Singhal
title: Head of Development at Biogen
msg: We'll be again looking at the totality of that to see if we can isolate a signal of clinical efficacy. I think we'll be very disciplined in how we look at that. You can expect that we'll be looking at that data very carefully, but with really being very disciplined about what the next step is, because that is what this proof of concept is designed for, if and how we get to phase III.

speaker: Chris Viehbacher
title: President and CEO at Biogen
msg: I think, you know, one of the interesting here is that, again, there's just no precedent here, right? You know, in designing the study, I think, Priya, it'd be fair to say we basically looked at what we did with amyloid trials, right? We've got the 18-month follow-up. We're looking at a similar population because that's the only thing we knew. We're gonna be discovering an awful lot in this study. Certainly, you know, you wanna see the right reduction in tau and tau PET results will be important. Obviously, you know, can you see some movement on cognition? I think that's where the totality of information is gonna be.

speaker: Chris Viehbacher
title: President and CEO at Biogen
msg: You know, while we feel relatively confident being able to reduce the tau, nobody knows how long you have to reduce the tau for to get a benefit on cognition.
